blocks.content: A LimitRange sets minimum, maximum, and default resource values for individual containers within a namespace, the per-object counterpart to ResourceQuota's namespace-wide total.

Where ResourceQuota (covered in the previous topic) caps the sum across an entire namespace, LimitRange constrains each individual container or Pod on its own, its own min, max, and default resource values.

blocks.alt: Constraints on each individual container, not the namespace's total

blocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
    - default:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 256Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 250m
        memory: 128Mi
      type: Container

blocks.content: These two objects genuinely complement each other rather than overlapping, ResourceQuota answers "how much can this namespace use in total," LimitRange answers "how much can any single container within it use."

blocks.alt: A total versus a per-object constraint, two different, complementary questions

blocks.content: If a Pod spec does not specify its own resource requests or limits at all, a LimitRange can automatically inject sensible defaults, meaning even a carelessly written manifest still ends up with reasonable resource behavior, rather than none at all.

blocks.alt: Sensible defaults applied automatically, even to an incomplete manifest

blocks.content: 4. Preventing Any One Pod From Going Overboard
blocks.text: 4. Preventing Any One Pod From Going Overboard

blocks.content: The maximum side of a LimitRange stops a single Pod from requesting an unreasonably large amount of CPU or memory, even one within an otherwise-healthy ResourceQuota budget, a real safety net against a single misconfigured manifest.

blocks.alt: A ceiling on any single container, regardless of the namespace's overall budget

blocks.content: In practice, ResourceQuota and LimitRange are commonly used together, LimitRange keeps individual containers sane and within reasonable bounds, ResourceQuota keeps the namespace's overall total in check, two layers of protection working at different scopes.

blocks.alt: Two complementary layers of protection, working at different scopes together

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: LimitRange sets per-container min, max, and default resource values, the complement to ResourceQuota's namespace-wide total cap.
It can auto-inject sensible defaults for containers that specify none, and prevents any single Pod from requesting an unreasonable amount on its own.
